experimental_method: Static equilibrium cell (about 200 cm3, up to 100 MPa) with magnetic stirrer; water-rich phase sample depressurised and the liberated gas analysed by gas chromatography (TCD) to get total and individual hydrocarbon solubilities in pure water at 71 C.
uncertainties_stated: Solubility experimental uncertainty about +-5% (relative); pressure held constant within +-1%; trapped-water hydrocarbon content below 10 ppm mol; neglect of water in the liberated gas overestimates total solubility by about 2%.
quality_remarks: Rows marked a (5 and 2.5 MPa, 23.0 and 45.5 % methane, Table 3) were measured most probably in the three-phase region (hydrocarbon-liquid present), so solubility there is nearly independent of gas-phase composition. A solid triangle marker precedes 0.2183 (C1+C2, 20 MPa, 100.0 % methane) in Table 2 and is not explained. Temperature scale not stated. Whether total pressure includes water vapour is not stated.
needs_pass2_reason: Text layer was clean (no scan); every cell of Tables 2 and 3 matched the 300 dpi page image. Row labelled 100 printed without decimal in Table 3 and C1 0.466 at 75 MPa printed with three decimals; kept as printed. Mixtures: gas code ch4-c2h6 and ch4-n-c4h10; the first column is the water-free methane content of the hydrocarbon-rich phase in mol %. Pure-gas end rows (0.0 and 100) are binary systems. The alkane-rich phase is gas-like at 71 C except where footnote a applies. Sanity: solubility of methane increases with pressure at fixed composition; total solubility increases with methane content at each pressure; no anomalies except the 5 MPa a-flagged rows.
